newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends soft after pre-weekend adjusting.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends soft after pre-weekend adjusting.

text.p: Mexican 24-hour and 48-hour peso contracts softened near the close of trading Friday as players adjusted their positions ahead of the weekend, traders said.

"The session was very quiet. Dollars were in supply early on, when dealers sold them in the same-day market, and then in demand when they bought them at 24 hours and 48 hours before the close," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso MXAAA closed 0.1 centavos weaker at 7.8750/7.8800 per dollar, and its 24-hour stable mate ended 1.1 centavos weaker at 7.8700/7.8740.
The same-day peso earlier closed 2.95 centavos firmer at 7.8420/7.8475 per dollar.
Traders say that dealers tend to sell dollars in the same-day market on Fridays and then buy them back at 24 hours using pesos invested in the local money market over the weekend.
Traders said the market was calm in the wake of a report Thursday on third-quarter gross domestic product, which showed year-on-year real growth of 7.4 percent.
"The market received the GDP figure well and the beneficial effect was carried over to today's session," a trader said.
Traders said the market was also steady ahead of Banco de Mexico's report on inflation in the first half of November. The announcement was due after the close of trade.
A Reuters survey of brokerages, banks and research firms MXAAP showed an average forecast of a 0.87 percent rise in consumer prices.
Dealers said they expected some pressure on the peso because of normal month-end demand, but recent stability led them to expect that 48-hour contracts would find support at 7.95 per dollar.
